title: Erhu (two-string fiddle)
summary: The erhu is a Chinese fiddle with just two strings and no fingerboard. A six-sided wooden barrel, faced with snakeskin, rests on the player's thigh while a horsehair bow passes between the strings. Notes are made by touching the strings in the air and sliding, so the sound can sigh, sob or gallop.
howToPlay: Two strings climb the long neck; each coloured lane marks the finger place of one note, the lower notes on the inner string and the higher ones on the outer.
A bead slides down toward its finger place. Bow that note just as the bead lands.
Long notes show a tail: let them sing for their full length, as a bow would.
Start with the slow sighing line, then try the galloping figure and the rising-and-falling tune.
rules: The strings are tuned a fifth apart, here D and A, and the notes follow the D major scale.
A bow stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Long notes are judged at their start only.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The erhu belongs to the large family of Chinese bowed fiddles and has been played in village ensembles, street music and theatre for many centuries. Today it is heard as a solo voice and in orchestras, loved for glides that sound close to the human voice.
